general.q: Which town is located at the southernmost point of mainland Europe?
general.why: Tarifa is in southern Spain and is only about 14 kilometres from the coast of Morocco.

general.q: For which invention was the Scottish-born scientist Alexander Graham Bell granted a patent in 1876?
general.why: Bell's patent for the telephone is often cited as one of the most valuable in history.

general.q: Which of King Henry VIII’s six wives was the biological mother of Queen Elizabeth I?
general.why: Anne Boleyn was the mother of Elizabeth I, while Jane Seymour gave birth to the future Edward VI.

general.q: What is the main legume used to make the traditional Middle Eastern dip hummus?
general.why: The word 'hummus' literally means chickpea in Arabic.

general.q: At which English racecourse is the Derby, one of the five Classics of the Flat racing season, held annually?
general.why: The Derby at Epsom Downs was first run in 1780 and is the most prestigious of the five Classics.

pop.q: In Only Fools and Horses, which three-word phrase does Uncle Albert usually use to start his war stories?
pop.why: Uncle Albert famously annoyed Del and Rodney by starting every story with those three words.

pop.q: In the original 1980 arcade game Pac-Man, what is the name of the red ghost?
pop.why: Blinky is the leader of the ghosts; the others are named Pinky, Inky, and Clyde.

pop.q: Which actress played the 'Oxo Mum' in the long-running British television adverts from 1983 to 1999?
pop.why: Lynda Bellingham became a household name playing the mother in the popular Oxo family adverts.

pop.q: In the 1977 film Star Wars, which character is the pilot and captain of the Millennium Falcon?
pop.why: Han Solo won the ship from Lando Calrissian in a game of Sabacc before the events of the films.

pop.q: What was the name of the collectible animal figures launched in the UK in 1987 by the toy company Tomy?
pop.why: Sylvanian Families were woodland creature figures that lived in the fictional village of Sylvania.

music.q: Which band released the multi-platinum 1985 album 'Songs from the Big Chair'?
music.why: It featured the massive hits Shout and Everybody Wants to Rule the World.

music.q: Who defeated Gareth Gates to win the final of the first series of Pop Idol in February 2002?
music.why: Will Young won the final with 53% of the vote in one of the most-watched TV moments of 2002.

music.q: The 2006 viral music video for 'Here It Goes Again' featured which band dancing on eight treadmills?
music.why: The low-budget video was a viral sensation in the early days of YouTube.

music.q: Which band replaced The Stone Roses as Glastonbury headliners in 1995 after they pulled out?
music.why: Jarvis Cocker and his band stepped in to play a legendary set on the Pyramid Stage.

music.q: Which song was at the top of the UK Singles Chart on New Year's Day 1980?
music.why: The song, which features a school choir, spent five weeks at the top of the charts.

mix.q: Which British indie band released the critically acclaimed 1994 album 'Parklife'?
mix.why: The album helped define the Britpop era and won four Brit Awards.

mix.q: In the 1985 film 'Back to the Future', what speed must the DeLorean reach to travel through time?
mix.why: Doc Brown's time machine requires this specific speed to trigger the flux capacitor.

mix.q: Located in the Lake District, which is the largest natural lake in England?
mix.why: It is the largest natural lake in England, stretching for over 10 miles.

mix.q: In the sitcom 'Father Ted', what is the name of the fictional island where the priests live?
mix.why: Ted, Dougal, and Jack are exiled to this island off the coast of Ireland.

mix.q: What is the most abundant gas found in the Earth's atmosphere?
mix.why: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.

mix.q: Which British singer had a huge UK number one hit in 1987 with 'Never Gonna Give You Up'?
mix.why: This debut single was the best-selling single of 1987 in the UK.

mix.q: In the 'Harry Potter' books, what is the name of the village where Harry was born?
mix.why: It is the birthplace of Godric Gryffindor and the location of the Potters' house.

mix.q: Which English king was killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485?
mix.why: His death marked the end of the Wars of the Roses and the start of the Tudor dynasty.

mix.q: In the 'Sonic the Hedgehog' video games, what is the name of Sonic's two-tailed fox sidekick?
mix.why: Miles Prower, better known as Tails, first appeared in Sonic the Hedgehog 2.

mix.q: Which spirit is traditionally used as the base for a classic Mojito cocktail?
mix.why: This Cuban cocktail consists of white rum, sugar, lime juice, soda water, and mint.
